samples.summary: MemoryDocStore.setBlockType still injects an empty inline into a table block — the invariant the Yorkie store change just established is not honored by the sibling DocStore
samples.evidence: The diff changes `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1469, 1494) to `type !== 'table' && block.inlines.length === 0` because "a table node's children are its rows (`block.inlines` is always `[]`)". The other implementation of the same `DocStore.setBlockType` contract, `MemoryDocStore.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:260-264), still does `else if (block.inlines.length === 0) { block.inlines = [{ text: '', style: {} }]; }` with no table exclusion, so retyping a block to 'table' through the memory store (docs local store, slides/board text bodies, `Document.setBlockType` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:462) still produces a table block carrying a phantom inline. The two stores now disagree about the same document shape.

samples.summary: One remaining subtree-spanning `removeStyleByPath` call was not converted to the new node-scoped `removeNodeStyle` helper
samples.evidence: `removeNodeStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:262-281) documents that `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` "looks node-scoped but is not: that path range spans the node's whole subtree, and Yorkie applies the removal to every element node in it". The inline-style clear path at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1918 still does exactly that — `tree.removeStyleByPath([...blockPath, i], [...blockPath, i + 1], removeAttrs)` — and was left unconverted while the block, cell-style and cell-span sites were all migrated. Harmless only as long as an inline node's children are exclusively text nodes; any future element child inside an inline reintroduces the bug the helper exists to prevent.

samples.summary: Design doc still describes `applyCellSpan` clearing spans via `removeStyleByPath`, which the change replaced with the index-scoped `removeNodeStyle`
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-intent-preserving-edits.md:240 states "`applyCellSpan` uses `styleByPath` to set span values and `removeStyleByPath` to clear them". After the change, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2520 calls `removeNodeStyle(tree, cellPath, attrsToRemove)` (index range over the cell's opening tag), not `removeStyleByPath`. This is a nested design doc, so the top-level docs link/ref check does not cover it.

samples.summary: Design doc names a helper `removeCellNodeStyle` that does not exist; the shipped helper is the general `removeNodeStyle`
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md:184 says "Yorkie has no single-node removal, so `removeCellNodeStyle` (`yorkie-doc-store.ts`) converts the path to an index…". The function added by this change is `removeNodeStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:273), shared by the block-type, cell-style and cell-span paths, not a cell-specific helper. A reader grepping for the documented name finds nothing.

samples.summary: `writeDocsRoot` has a second caller that does not pass through the newly hardened `assertValidDocsBody`
samples.evidence: The new header/footer, inline and cell-style validation is applied only in `putContent` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:149). `DocumentCopyService` reaches the same writer directly at packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:174 (`writeDocsRoot(root as DocsYorkieRoot, content)`) with no validation. Its input is a `readDocsRoot` of an existing document, so today the shapes are already normalized — but any document persisted in a malformed shape before this change is copied through the writer unchecked, i.e. the guard is not on the writer boundary the comments claim to protect.
searchedFor: grep @Post in packages/backend/src/api/v1/*.controller.ts (checked document create takes no content)

finding.summary: New slide-inline guard accepts an inline with no `style`; every downstream reader dereferences `inline.style` unconditionally, so such a stored inline crashes canvas layout and PPTX export for every viewer
finding.evidence: The new `assertValidSlideInlines` only rejects a *non-object* `style` (`inline.style !== undefined && inline.style !== null && typeof !== 'object'`), so `{ text: 'x' }` with no style passes. Consumers that the diff does not show: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:777` reads `inline.style.image` unconditionally inside `measureSegments` (TypeError on undefined), and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:291` (`rPrXml`) reads `s.bold` on the same value straight off `runToXml` (`text.ts:226`). The docs arm of the very same controller requires a present object style (`docs-content.controller.ts:437`), so a payload rejected through `blocks[*]` is accepted through a deck's text bodies/notes/layout placeholders and then breaks readers rather than the caller. Fix belongs on the new guard (require an object `style`, or make readers default it).

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is not present in the code. It states the new slide-inline guard "only rejects a non-object style, so { text: 'x' } with no style passes" and is then stored, crashing readers. The actual function is normalizeSlideInlines (the name assertValidSlideInlines appears nowhere in source, only in prior review artifacts under .agent-review/), and it contains a branch the finding omits entirely: at docs-content.controller.ts:778-780, `if (inline.style === undefined || inline.style === null) { inline.style = {}; continue; }`. A missing style is REPAIRED in place to {}; only a present non-object style 400s (:782-786). The repair reaches storage: assertValidSlidesBody(body) (:153) mutates the parsed body in place, and that same object is passed to writeSlidesRoot(root, body as SlidesDocument) (:193) and echoed back at :198 — there is no clone between validation and write. All three routes the finding names converge on assertValidSlideBlocks, which calls the repair at :706: text bodies (:677), slide notes (:557), and layout placeholders/staticElements (:513 -> assertValidNestedElement:595 -> assertValidElementData:612 -> :619/:623). Therefore no inline lacking style can be persisted through this endpoint, and the cited consumers (docs/src/view/layout.ts measureSegments, slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts rPrXml) are never handed such a value from this path. The finding's own prescribed fix ("require an object style, or make readers default it") is already implemented as the defaulting option at the guard itself; the documented asymmetry with the docs arm at :437 is an intentional alternative remedy (rationale at :740-747: avoiding a 400 on a GET->edit->PUT round-trip of decks that already store style-less inlines), not a hole.

searchedFor: grep inlines in packages/slides/src and packages/frontend/src/app/slides
finding.summary: The guard tolerates a slide block with `inlines` entirely absent, but the shared docs layout engine dereferences `block.inlines` unconditionally — the same crash class the guard was added to close is still reachable by simply omitting the field
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideInlines` returns early for `undefined`/`null` (documented as legitimate for placeholder bodies), and `assertValidSlideBlocks` never requires the field. Out-of-diff consumers: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:152/154` (`resolveBlockInlines` returns `block.inlines` / calls `block.inlines.map`) and `measureSegments` at `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:767` iterates `inlines.length` — undefined propagates to a TypeError. Nothing normalizes slide blocks on read: `packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts` has no `blocks`/`inlines` handling, and `writeSlidesRoot` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93`) stores the JSON verbatim. Backend spec line 1008 ('accepts a slide text block that omits id/inlines') shows the tolerance is deliberate, so the fix is either defaulting `inlines` to `[]` at the writer/reader or rejecting the omission.

verdict.reason: The finding describes an `assertValidSlideInlines` that returns early (leaving `inlines` absent) so an omitted field is stored verbatim and later crashes `resolveBlockInlines`/`measureSegments`. That code is not present. The actual helper is `normalizeSlideInlines` (docs-content.controller.ts:752), which for an absent value assigns `block.inlines = []` (:756-760) and for an absent inline style assigns `inline.style = {}` (:778-781), throwing only for present-but-wrong values. It is invoked for every block the walk visits (:706), and the walk covers text bodies (:619, :623, :633), slide notes (:557), layout placeholders/static elements (:493-515, :595-599), group children (:636-641) and nested table-cell blocks (:708-721). The repair is on the same object that is persisted and echoed: putContent validates `body` (:153) and then passes that same reference to writeSlidesRoot (:193) and returns it (:198); writeSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:97-109) bulk-assigns those already-repaired objects. The spec the finding cites as evidence of deliberate tolerance (spec:1008) only asserts no 400; the neighbouring test (spec:1122-1147) asserts `blocks[0].inlines` === [] and `blocks[1].inlines[0].style` === {} on the body handed to the writer, i.e. normalization is explicitly verified. Hence the described bypass to packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts is not reachable via this endpoint.
